messages:
Alice C (Sales): Heads-up — POC kickoff with Aurora Bank on Wed. They require air-gapped on‑prem eval. Main blocker: no persistent jumpbox creds allowed. Need a clear bootstrap runbook + acceptance criteria and pricing for offline packaging. Can eng/security/solutions weigh in?
Ben (Eng-ML): We can do it, but we need a defined transport & short-lived bootstrap creds. Typical approach: signed bundle + one-time token delivered out-of-band.
Carol (Solutions): Noted. Customer cannot provision a public-facing jumpbox at all. Proposed: operator-run install from USB with ephemeral admin creds (TTL 1–4h).
Diane (Security): Requirements from our side: signed artifacts, SBOM, attestations, and defined key custody. Who holds the signing key? HSM or Redwood KMS?
Tom (Aurora IT): Clarification — we cannot use Redwood KMS. All keys must be customer-managed and remain offline. Also need chain-of-custody for any USB transport.
Eric (Legal): They asked about liability for physical transport (USB). We need SOW language and liability limits.
Ben (Eng-ML): Draft bootstrap checklist (sketch):
````
1) Customer generates operator keypair (operator.pub) offline
2) Redwood builds signed bundle + SBOM, produces SHA256 manifest
3) Bundle + manifest exported to physical media (USB) and hand-delivered
4) Operator runs `./install.sh --bundle bundle.tar.gz --trust operator.pub`
5) Installer requests a one-time bootstrap token from Redwood ops (delivered separately) valid N hours
6) Post-boot: local certs generated, optional registry of node when network allowed
````
Ben (Eng-ML): We should decide token TTL. Security tradeoff: shorter TTL better but operationally harder.
Carol (Solutions): Customer preference: minimal window. Can we do 1h?
Diane (Security): Recommend 1h TTL + operator MFA for starting install. Also require local audit logs shipped to their SIEM (no egress to Redwood).
Tom (Aurora IT): On USB transport — we require tamper-evident seals and a manifest signed by Redwood. Can you provide signed checksums?
Ben (Eng-ML): Yes — we can provide SHA256 manifest signed with our release key. If they insist on HSM-signed keys on our side, need to confirm ops.
Fiona (Finance): Pricing for offline POC packaging: one-time packaging & signing fee of $5k, plus per-node offline license $1k/mo. POC discounts possible.
Alice C (Sales): Pricing noted. Also they asked about upgrade cadence — how often do we publish delta bundles for air-gapped installs?
Carol (Solutions): Proposed cadence: quarterly feature bundles + monthly security patches (delta bundles). Emergency CVE patches out-of-band.
Diane (Security): We must include cert rotation guidance and a documented process for applying security patches offline. They requested max 8-week patch commitment.
Ben (Eng-ML): We can commit to 8-week security patch cadence. Feature releases can remain quarterly. We'll provide backport windows for critical fixes.
Tom (Aurora IT): Good. Also need a rollback plan in case a bundle fails. What’s the fallback?
Ben (Eng-ML): Installer will snapshot state before applying. Rollback supported via `./install.sh --rollback <snapshot>`; we’ll document failure modes.
Carol (Solutions): Operational acceptance criteria for POC (customer asked):
- install completes without external network
- services come up within N minutes
- can run a canonical inference workload within expected latency (we will provide perf script)
- SBOM and signed manifest verified locally
Diane (Security): Add: successful local audit log generation and verified key custody steps.
Eric (Legal): I’ll draft SOW addendum for physical transport liability, acceptance criteria, and support SLAs during POC.
Alice C (Sales): Action items:
- Ben: produce runbook draft + signed-manifest workflow (owner)
- Carol: confirm packaging fee + distribution notes for SOW
- Diane: list security reqs for acceptance criteria
- Eric: SOW wording for USB transport & liability
- Fiona: finalize POC price and per-node license terms
- Tom: confirm internal chain-of-custody process and operator contact
Alice C (Sales): Target: send runbook + SOW draft to customer by EOD Monday. @Ben @Eric @Diane please ack if doable. :thumbsup:
Ben (Eng-ML): ACK, will have runbook draft by EOD Monday.
Diane (Security): ACK, will provide security checklist and TTL recommendation.
Eric (Legal): ACK, I’ll draft SOW addendum and circulate for review.
